headline: Hiring a Bathroom Remodeling Contractor: What to Review Before You Sign
articleBody:
Planning a primary or guest bath update takes more than picking tile samples. Here is a clear guide on evaluating quotes and establishing project scope.

Key Benefits
A properly planned bathroom remodel enhances daily routines, increases storage, and upgrades ventilation to protect against chronic humidity.

Process Breakdown
Begin with detailed measurements and an inspection of your subflooring, framing, and rough plumbing. Next, confirm layout requirements and permitting needs before any demolition starts. Quality installations include verified waterproof assemblies, code-compliant ventilation, and exact plumbing rough-ins before setting vanities, tubs, or custom tile.

Real Examples
Updating an older Salt Lake Valley home from an acrylic tub surround to a walk-in tile shower requires checking framing integrity, relocating supply valves, and confirming the drain line size can support a modern shower setup without backing up.

Questions to Ask Before You Decide
Always ask your contractor how they address concealed rot, who handles permitting and trade inspections, and how material lead times get tracked before demo starts.
